sections.name: Introductions
sections.description: Getting to know one another, and why we are here.

items.title: Basic Introduction
content: Share your name, where you live, and what drew you here.

items.title: Partcipation Reason
content: Why did you decide to participate in this conversation?

sections.name: Community Norms
sections.description: These are a set of norms that we all agree on. These will set the tone of the conversation and ensure that it is welcoming and constructive.

items.title: Be curious and listen.
content: Be open to others’ experiences and ready to learn from them. Conversation is as much about listening and absorbing others’ perspectives as it is about sharing your own.
We are here to explain and understand each other, not to convince others to change their minds.

items.title: Be respectful and do not judge.
content: Judgement is natural, but prevents respect. Strive to set your judgement aside to make others feel respected and valued.
Give others the benefit of the doubt. Do not make assumptions about others’ views and perspectives.

items.title: Seek common ground.
content: Look for shared values and areas of agreement, while staying curious about differing beliefs and opinions.
You will encounter diverging views. That is expected and hoped for. Treat everyone with civility and do not push back on others’ views.

items.title: Embrace and welcome authenticity.
content: Share what is important to you, speak from experience, and welcome others doing the same.

sections.name: Dialogue
sections.description: This is a time to understand one anothers' perspectives and build trust.

items.title: Purpose
content: What sense of purpose/mission/duty guides you in your life? How does this inform your perspective on dfsafdasfdas?

sections.name: Exploration
sections.description: An exploration of a topic: meant to generate ideas, questions, and unknowns.

items.title: Topic Background Recommendations
content: Focus on objective facts that are relevant to the conversation.
Provide accredited citations.
Be careful with framing: do not frame the facts as benefitting one side or the other.
The goal with facts is to generate a shared reality, and to create a starting point
Be careful: facts can be triggering. If people cannot agree on the facts, that can also be a starting point for the conversation. How people feel is most important.

sections.name: Evaluation
sections.description: Coalescing around ideas, perhaps coming to an agreement or making a decision.

items.title: Future Actions
content: How might the perspectives raised today necessitate future actions or change?

items.title: Needed Change
content: What needs to change in our institutions, systems, and society so that everyone can flourish?

sections.name: Conclusion
sections.description: A time to reflect on the conversation and appreciate fellow participants.

items.title: Conversation reflections
content: How do we each feel about the conversation we’ve just had?
What did you learn about diverging perspectives and views?
What might you take away from this conversation?
guidance: Each participant chooses one of the reflection prompts to respond to.
